stories.notes: Story has empty acceptance criteria and spans three platforms (GO, UP, MX) implying significant complexity. Openspec needed first to elaborate requirements, define ACs, and propose technical depth for live preview across platforms. Speckit then reviews openspec output to add testability criteria, security checks (preview token handling, cross-origin iframe sandboxing), and edge cases (concurrent edits, preview staleness, platform-specific rendering). Priority high due to cross-platform scope and zero existing spec.

agentContributions.notes: Novel capability — Contentstack Live Preview integration. The attachment point is useContent (236 callers), the central hook all content components consume via getContentByKey. Live Preview SDK must plug into this hook so every downstream component automatically reflects CMS editor changes without a full page reload. No acceptance criteria were provided; VCs derived from the description and the Contentstack Live Preview SDK's expected behavior, stopping at our side of the Contentstack API boundary.

Openspec provided empty acceptance criteria with valuable context about the useContent hook (236 callers) and getContentByKey as the integration point. I authored all ACs from scratch based on the story description and openspec's notes. Key areas covered: (1) Core live-preview update behavior (AC-1, AC-9, AC-11), (2) Backward compatibility when preview is inactive (AC-2, AC-8), (3) Error/failure handling for SDK absence, malformed data, connection errors, and invalid tokens (AC-3, AC-5, AC-10, AC-12), (4) Rapid-update resilience (AC-4), (5) Session lifecycle — reverting to published content when preview ends (AC-6), (6) Accessibility for dynamic content changes (AC-7). I could not review the actual file contents of useContent.ts, contentstack.ts, ContentstackContext.tsx, contentCard.ts, or ContentstackLink.tsx — the ACs are based solely on the story title, description, and openspec's notes. If the file contents reveal additional integration points or constraints, some ACs may need refinement.

coordinatorReview.reviewNotes: Both agents contributed non-overlapping value: openspec identified the critical integration point (useContent/getContentByKey, 236 callers) and provided architectural context; speckit attempted to author 11 acceptance criteria covering core behavior, backward compatibility, error handling, rapid updates, session lifecycle, and accessibility. However, two issues require human review. (1) AC persistence discrepancy: speckit claims to have authored all ACs from scratch, yet acceptanceChanged is false and the story still shows acceptanceCriteria: []. Either the ACs were written to a separate spec document not reflected in this record, or they were not persisted — either way the deliverable state is ambiguous. (2) Neither agent reviewed actual source files (useContent.ts, contentstack.ts, ContentstackContext.tsx, contentCard.ts, ContentstackLink.tsx), which speckit itself acknowledges. For a high-priority cross-platform story (GO, UP, MX) with zero prior spec, the ACs are based solely on the story title/description and openspec's notes rather than verified code structure. Recommend human review to confirm AC persistence and validate ACs against actual source files before implementation.
